From Tomorrow

Read on Kindle ↗ Goodreads

About the book

The Story

The train line is closing in three days. Hina knows this. What she doesn't know is why the note she just found beneath her seat is signed by someone she has never met — and dated tomorrow.

Someone named Ray is leaving her messages from a day she hasn't lived yet. And somehow, she is leaving him messages from a day he hasn't reached.

With the line's final hours counting down, the notes between them grow more urgent. Something is going to happen. Something that cannot be undone.

And the only people who can stop it are two strangers who have never once been on the same train.

From Tomorrow is a story about time, loss, and the moments we almost miss.

Sakura Slice Café

桜スライス・カフェ

Somewhere in Cairo, there is a café that was never just a café.

Read on Kindle ↗ Goodreads

About the book

The Story

Somewhere in Cairo, there is a café that was never just a café.

Sakura Slice Café began as an email — a simple message sent to a friend who was tired of carrying the world alone. It grew into a place: not quite physical, not quite imaginary, but entirely real to everyone who found their way through its doors.

In thirteen quiet stories, you will meet the people who came to the café and left something behind — or found something they didn't know they were missing. A boy who already knew how to be kind. A girl who forgot how to cry. A man who rediscovered his language through the taste of something sweet. An artist who drew everyone when no one was watching. A mother who came prepared to love both her sons equally, in the same breath.

Each story is small. Each one carries something.

Sakura Slice Café is a book about being seen. About the ordinary magic of a place that asks nothing of you except that you come in, sit down, and stay as long as you need.

Your table is already waiting for you.

The Perfect Sunrise

完璧な日の出

Every morning, Hikari chases the perfect sunrise. Every morning, it eludes her. Then one evening, a photograph falls from the sky — already developed, already perfect, and dated tomorrow.

Follow on Goodreads

About the book

The Story

It is signed by someone named Kai. Someone who knows her name. Someone who hasn't arrived yet.

As a mysterious fog tightens its grip on her coastal town, the photographs keep coming — each one more urgent than the last. Hikari doesn't know who Kai is. But she is beginning to suspect that finding him before the next sunrise matters more than she could have imagined.

Some messages travel across time. Some sunrises change everything.

The Perfect Sunrise is about memory, loss, and the quiet truth that the people we love never truly leave us — even when we can no longer see them.

The Author

About Me

I am an Egyptian boy who had always dreamt of magic — the kind I'd always wished I could show everyone.

By day, I work as a Project Manager and assistant lecturer at university. In between, I write books about train stations and cafés and sunrises, and I build websites that try to feel like places worth visiting.

I grew up lost in books — Rick Riordan's mythologies, Brandon Sanderson's worlds, Cassandra Clare's shadowhunters. They were the ones who made me believe that stories could do something real to a person. They made me want to write.

I am also slowly, happily learning Japanese — one word at a time, one sentence at a time, one story at a time.
